clue.text: Just clever, having no need of book

indicators.note: doing without something means the book's letter is dropped from the word for clever

parts.note: a bright pupil is a clever one

explanation.surface: A verdict that someone is smart enough to manage without consulting any book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like 'merely' but is the definition, in the sense of fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A just decision is a right one: both describe what is morally fair and correct.

clue.text: Tale of a debt collector, maybe, involving island warehouse

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the tale surrounds the letter for island

parts.words: Tale of a debt collector, maybe
parts.note: a repo man repossesses goods, so his tale is a repo story

explanation.surface: A story about a bailiff on an island, set in a storage depot.
explanation.definitionFit: A repository is a place where things are stored, like a warehouse.

clue.text: Opening section of book cut up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are written from bottom to top
cut means trimmed, losing its last letter

parts.note: a page is a section of a book

explanation.surface: The first part of a book is chopped up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' takes the last letter off PAGE, giving PAG; 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A gap is a space or opening, as in a gap in a fence.

clue.text: Bird hurried after half of this

indicators.note: after places the word for hurried behind the half
the first two of the four letters of this

parts.note: rush means hurried, here in the past tense sense 'rushed' read as a verb form

explanation.surface: A bird darting off after half of something.
explanation.definitionFit: The thrush is a songbird, such as the song thrush or mistle thrush.

clue.text: Problem backing the French — quite without oomph — in raunchy US show

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word for problem is read from its end

parts.note: a rub is a difficulty, as in 'there's the rub'
les is French for 'the' (plural)

indicators.note: without signals that the word for oomph is removed from 'quite'

parts.note: taken as written before the removal
'it' is sex appeal or oomph

explanation.surface: A grumble about the French being rather flat in some saucy American stage act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns RUB into BUR; 'without' takes IT out of QUITE, leaving QUE.
explanation.definitionFit: American burlesque was a variety show famous for striptease, hence raunchy.

clue.text: City area sadly variable with little good in it

indicators.note: in it means the letter for good goes inside the rearranged word
sadly means badly, so the letters of variable are rearranged

parts.note: G is the short form of good

explanation.surface: A district of a city with unsettled character and not much good in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Belgravia is a wealthy district of central London.
explanation.definitionFit: Belgravia is an area of London, the city, known for grand houses and embassies.

clue.text: Resistance, with support, absorbing pressure without delay

definitions.note: a phrase standing for an adjective: a rapid response is one given without delay

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

indicators.note: absorbing means soaking up, so the word for support takes in the pressure letter

parts.note: aid is help or support
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Physics notes on a resistor and a brace that quickly soak up pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid means fast or quick, happening immediately rather than late.

clue.text: Support an entry for Chaucer in "Early English Style"

indicators.note: in puts the leg, an and first letter of Chaucer between the two Es

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for both early and English
a leg supports a table or chair

indicators.note: the entry, or first letter, of the name Chaucer

explanation.surface: An encyclopedia entry on Chaucer under the heading 'Early English Style'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Early English Style' looks like a single architectural term; the definition is only 'Style'.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegance is grace and refinement, what we call style.

clue.text: Lives dangerously after living once on river of molten metal

indicators.note: after puts the jumbled lives behind the old word for living

parts.note: quick meant alive in old English, as in 'the quick and the dead'

indicators.note: dangerously signals the letters of lives are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone living recklessly on a river of liquid metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Quicksilver is the old name for mercury, a metal that is liquid at room temperature.

clue.text: Some pristine development held up as Paradise

indicators.note: in a down entry, held up means the hidden run is read upwards, backwards
some of these words gives the letters, a run hidden inside them

explanation.surface: A pristine new building scheme delayed but sold as heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' shows a hidden run, NEDE across 'pristine development'; 'held up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Eden is the garden of Genesis, the original paradise.

clue.text: It fixes where you find crossword, say, with some speed

parts.note: a crossword is printed in a newspaper, a paper
a clip is a fast pace, as in 'at a good clip'

explanation.surface: Someone describing a gadget that repairs things, found next to the puzzle page and working quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: A paperclip holds sheets together, so it is something that fastens or fixes them.

clue.text: Refugee with no time at all for material

indicators.note: having none means the time letters are taken out of the material

parts.note: textile is a woven material or fabric
T is the abbreviation for time, and 'at all' asks for every one, both Ts

explanation.surface: A displaced person with no spare moment to look for cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no time at all' removes both Ts from TEXTILE, not just one.
explanation.definitionFit: An exile is someone forced from their homeland, much like a refugee.

clue.text: One gets ready for taking these steps to provide relief?

definitions.text: One gets ready for taking these steps to provide relief?

parts.words: One gets ready for taking these steps to provide relief?
parts.note: 'ready' is slang for cash: a walker collects money from backers for each stage of a charity hike

explanation.surface: Someone preparing to take measures that will ease a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets ready' reads as preparing, but 'ready' is money, and 'steps' are literal paces; 'relief' is charity aid.
explanation.definitionFit: On a charity hike, backers pledge cash for the distance covered, raising money for relief causes.

clue.text: Business site, apparently no longer postponed, encountering obstruction

parts.note: postponed plans are 'on ice'; taken off, they are humorously 'off ice'
a block is an obstruction or barrier

explanation.surface: A work location is now going ahead but hits a snag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On ice' means shelved, so its opposite reads OFF ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: An office block is a building of offices, a place where business is done.

clue.text: Looking back, covering a lot of historic city in particular

indicators.note: covering means the word for particular wraps around the shortened city

parts.note: a respect is a particular or detail, as in 'in every respect'

indicators.note: a lot of means most of, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: Troy is the ancient city of Homer's Iliad

explanation.surface: A retrospective survey of an ancient city, done in detail.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrospect is a review of the past, the act of looking back.

clue.text: Dispute ignoring opening of firm

indicators.note: leaving out the first letter of the word meaning firm

parts.note: stiff means firm, rigid

explanation.surface: A disagreement that overlooks how a company began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like a company, but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff is a petty quarrel, a minor dispute.

clue.text: Zero energy around start of play — becoming too energetic?

parts.note: O looks like the figure zero

indicators.note: around means the word for energy wraps the opening of a play

parts.note: verve is energy, vigour
Act I is the first part of a play

explanation.surface: A lethargic actor at the curtain-up who then gets far too lively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of play' is ACT I, not P.
explanation.definitionFit: Overactive means busier or livelier than normal, energetic to excess.

clue.text: Have another look at bird by a quarry

parts.note: a ree is a female ruff, a wading bird
X stands for by, as in 3 by 4
a mine is a quarry or pit

explanation.surface: Taking a second glance at a bird near a quarry.
explanation.walkthrough: X means 'by' as in multiplication or dimensions.
explanation.definitionFit: To study or inspect something a second time is to have another look at it.

clue.text: A lot of sadness about hospital department in Italian resort

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shortened sorrow goes around the department
a lot of means most of, so the final letter goes

parts.note: sorrow is sadness
ENT is ear, nose and throat, a hospital department

explanation.surface: Much grief about a hospital ward at an Italian holiday town.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorrento is a seaside town on the Bay of Naples, a popular resort.

clue.text: Hymn producing historic shock?

definitions.meaning: a well-known Christian hymn by Augustus Toplady
playfully, an age-old jolt: a rock is a shock, and 'of ages' makes it ancient

explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' here means rock, as in 'it rocked me'.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names a famous church song, and read literally it suggests a jolt from long ago.

clue.text: Finished disguise, except the front

indicators.note: everything but the first letter of the word for disguise is kept

parts.note: a cover is a disguise or false identity

explanation.surface: A spy whose disguise is done with, apart from the façade.
explanation.definitionFit: Over means ended or completed, as in 'the game is over'.

clue.text: Try to get off with trophy, seizing lid

indicators.note: seizing means grasping, so the cup closes round the hat

parts.note: a cup is a trophy
lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: Making off with a trophy and grabbing its cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get off with' is British slang for to pull, start a romance.
explanation.definitionFit: To chat up is to flirt with someone, hoping to start a romance.

clue.text: Mother's absurd dressed in beachwear

indicators.note: dressed means arranged or put in order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mum looks ridiculous wearing her holiday outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absurd' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'dressed' rearranges MOTHERS and ABSURD together.
explanation.definitionFit: Bermuda shorts are knee-length casual shorts worn on holiday, especially at the seaside.

clue.text: Soldiers retaining force would be inappropriate

indicators.note: retaining means holding on to, so the soldiers contain the letter for force

parts.note: a unit is a body of soldiers
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: Troops keeping force on would be improper.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfit means unsuitable or not appropriate, as in 'unfit for purpose'.

clue.text: Opening for independent political party coming up in Asian island

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the letters are read upwards
the first letter of the word independent

parts.note: Lab is short for the UK Labour Party

explanation.surface: A chance for an independent candidate as a party rises on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Bali is an Indonesian island in Asia.

clue.text: Embellish even choices from garden?

explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of garden are A, D and N; offered as choices they read A, D OR N.

clue.text: Principled purchases in market rated adversely

clue.text: A couple of fifties provides the sum

explanation.surface: Two fifty-pound notes cover the whole bill.

explanation.walkthrough: BOTTLE is British slang for nerve or guts.

parts.note: a plot is the story line
